notes: Brackets: the 2025 Tax Rate Table prints no bracket schedule below 100,000, only tax by income row for each status; PDF page 7 (T-7) prints the rest: 'If line 17 of Form PIT-1 (Taxable Income) is over $100,000 use the following table to compute your tax.' Single 4,356 plus 4.9% over 100,000 up to 210,000, then 9,746 plus 5.9% over 210,000. Married filing jointly and head of household 4,087 plus 4.9% over 100,000 up to 315,000, then 14,622 plus 5.9% over 315,000. Married filing separately 4,492 plus 4.9% over 100,000 up to 157,500, then 7,310 plus 5.9% over 157,500. The surviving spouse uses the joint column (T-1 to T-7 footnote). Below 100,000 the rates and starts are derived from the table: tested at each row's midpoint they reproduce all 1,001 rows for all four statuses to within rounding, and moving any one start by 100, or any one rate by 0.1%, breaks the fit.

Brackets, the printed bases over 100,000: each base on T-7 is the table's last row (99,900 to 100,000, midpoint 99,950), not the tax at 100,000. The schedule's arithmetic gives 4,358 single, 4,089 joint and head of household, 4,494.50 separate at 100,000, so the printed section runs 2 (2.50 separate) lower at every income over 100,000. Those rows cannot go in derivation.table_rows: the validator allows 1 dollar. The 99,900 row is there for every status, and the 4.9% and 5.9% figures and the starts 210,000, 315,000 and 157,500 are printed. The top bases check by hand: 4,356 + 4.9% of 110,000 = 9,746; 4,087 + 4.9% of 215,000 = 14,622; 4,492 + 4.9% of 57,500 = 7,309.50, printed 7,310.
Forms read (rule 0): PIT-1, PIT-ADJ, PIT-RC and PIT-B return forms, and the Tax Rate Table. Still not in the sources: PIT-CR, PIT-S, and the PIT-RC and PIT-B instructions.

Base: Form PIT-1 starts from line 9, 'FEDERAL ADJUSTED GROSS INCOME. (from federal Form 1040 or 1040SR, line 11)'. Line 17: 'NEW MEXICO TAXABLE INCOME. Add lines 9, 10 and 11, then subtract lines 12, 13, 14, and 15. Cannot be less than zero'. Line 10 adds back state and local taxes for itemizers; line 11 is the PIT-ADJ additions; line 12 is the 'Federal standard or itemized deduction amount (from federal Form 1040, line 12'; line 15 is the PIT-ADJ deductions and exemptions. The form has no line for anything the federal return subtracts after line 12.

Standard deduction: New Mexico has no amount of its own in the sources. Line 12 takes 'the allowable federal standard deduction from federal Form 1040 or 1040SR, line 12' or 'the allowable federal itemized deductions' (PDF page 25). No dollar figure is printed, so no standard_deduction entry is recorded.

Personal exemption: no amount printed. 'Deduction amounts for personal exemptions are suspended for tax years 2018 through 2025 by the Federal Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.' (PDF page 22, Line 5.) The exemption count on line 5 still drives the low- and middle-income exemption.

Hidden text: the PDF text layers of both booklets, and so both converted texts, hold editors' working notes that are not on the printed page. Rendered, PIT-ADJ pages 5 and 7 and PIT-1 pages 22, 25 and 27 do not show them: the 'HB 252 Section 8 TY 2025 Change' box with '$1,0002,500', the sentence barring the net capital gains deduction with the Venture Capital Investments Act credit, the HB-0252 Section 32 note on armed forces retirement pay, 'Need to determine if this act has been extended or has lapsed.', the HB-6 extract, and a note 'Remove A taxpayer may not claim the deduction ...'. None of it is recorded as a rule.

Age 65 or blind: Table 1 prints one column for joint, head of household and surviving spouse (PIT-ADJ page 5); PIT-1 page 27 names only 'a joint return', and the table is used. Recorded twice, as age_65_exemption and blind_exemption, because 'The Department allows only one deduction per person.' (PIT-ADJ page 4.) The printed examples check: joint AGI 35,000 gives 6,000 each; joint AGI 28,000 gives 8,000 each.

Low- and middle-income exemption: one rule in the booklet, recorded as three entries because the schema's phase_out_rate holds one rate. Factors: 0.15 single; 0.10 joint, surviving spouse, head of household; 0.20 separate. The printed ceilings are where line 6 reaches zero: 20,000 + 2,500/0.15 = 36,666.67; 30,000 + 2,500/0.10 = 55,000; 15,000 + 2,500/0.20 = 27,500.

Social Security: PIT-ADJ line 25 and Table 2; second document, the agency web page, which words the limits as 'less than $100,000', 'under $150,000' and 'under $75,000'. The booklet's 'does not exceed' and Example 1 ('not above $100,000') are used, so AGI exactly at the limit keeps the exemption. The web page is a 2022 statement. PIT-1 page 27 also lists the exemption.

Pensions, IRA and employer-plan distributions, Roth conversions: Form PIT-ADJ lists 28 lines and none is for pensions, IRAs or employer plans, other than armed forces retirement pay (line 24), Railroad Retirement (line 10), retirement income from employment inside tribal boundaries (lines 11, 11a, 11b), and the age 100 exemption (line 12). PIT-ADJ instructions page 1: 'If an item is not listed, it is not a valid New Mexico addition, exemption, or deduction for this schedule.' Roth conversions are not mentioned anywhere: not found in the booklet.

Other states' government pensions, New York State's included: not found as a rule of their own, so no public_pension_other_state relief exists, and New York is named nowhere in the sources. Form PIT-B line 3 is 'Pensions, annuities, social security, and lump-sum distributions', with no split by payer, and its NOTE says 'Resident taxpayers including persons physically present in New Mexico 185 days or more, must allocate all income and deductions on lines 1, 2, 3, and 7 in full to New Mexico.' Line 20 NOTE (instructions PDF page 28): 'if you receive a pension from your former California employer and you now reside in New Mexico, California may not tax your retirement income. Because you are now a New Mexico resident, your retirement income is taxable in New Mexico.'
Own and federal government pensions: not found as a relief. Retiree withholding contacts appear at PIT-1 pages 20-21 and nothing there changes the tax.

Credits for people 65 or older, Form PIT-RC: property tax rebate at modified gross income of 16,000 or less (line 17c, at most 250, or 125 if married filing separately); refundable medical care credit (line 23, 'See PIT-RC instructions', which are not in the sources). Low income comprehensive tax rebate at modified gross income of 36,000 or less; its Table 1 is in those instructions too.

Other PIT-ADJ items, no dollar cap or not for planning, in notes only: Section 529 contributions (line 15; addition on line 3), New Mexico net operating loss (line 8), Medical Care Savings Account (line 14), National Guard life insurance reimbursement (line 20), refunds of state and local tax (line 21), non-resident USPHS pay (line 22), liquor license lessor deduction (line 23, up to 50,000), cannabis business expenses (line 26).

Credit for taxes paid to another state: PIT-1 line 20 and worksheet (PDF pages 28, 31). Lump-sum distributions: PIT-1 line 19 and worksheet (PDF pages 27, 28, 30), available only with federal Form 4972.
No surtax is printed. No recapture: the Tax Rate Table's top section is base plus rate on the excess, with no step that takes back the lower brackets.
Indexing: 'inflation', 'indexed', 'adjusted annually' and 'cost of living' appear nowhere in the booklets or the Tax Rate Table.
Settlement 2026-11-07: age_65_exemption and blind_exemption steps: A said 8 rows from 'over 30,000', B said 9 rows with an 8,000 row from 0; PIT-ADJ page 5 Table 1 prints nine rows; B.

Settlement 2026-11-07: social_security.treatment: A said relief, B said exempt; PIT-ADJ page 7 limits it by AGI and Example 2 says no part qualifies above the limit, so relief (the schema's 'exempt' has no income limit).

Settlement 2026-11-07: medical care exemption: A said an all_income relief, B said a deduction of type other; PIT-ADJ pages 5-6 say a flat $3,000 at $28,000 or more of medical expenses; B, because it is a flat amount tied to medical spending, not an age relief against income.

Settlement 2026-11-07: tribal income: A said all_income for the person, B said wages, public and private pensions; PIT-ADJ page 3 says 'your income is exempt' and adds 'including retirement or pension income'; A, with B's not_covered.
Settlement 2026-11-07: U.S. obligations covers: A said interest and dividends, B said interest; PIT-ADJ page 3 'You may deduct dividends from mutual funds invested in U.S. government obligations'; A.
Settlement 2026-11-07: 40% gains deduction applies_to: A said other, B said long_term; PIT-ADJ page 5 limits it to 'the sale of a business'; A.
Settlement 2026-11-07: personal exemption: A said notes only, B said an entry of amount 0; PIT-1 page 22 prints no amount; A.
Settlement 2026-11-07: Venture Capital Investments Act bar: A and B both recorded it; it is hidden text, not on rendered PIT-ADJ page 5, and hidden text on PIT-1 page 27 says 'Remove'; dropped.
Settlement 2026-11-07: brackets: A and B said empty, the rate tables not in the sources; the 2025 Tax Rate Table, archived after their readings, prints them; derived from its rows.
Settlement 2026-11-07: added by the settler: relief net_capital_gains_cap, because the capital_gains section has no field for the printed 2,500 limit.
